cases.name: signal-250-pins-seeded
cases.readme:
# Mendeley x86 CFG subgraphs (signal, 250 blocks), pipeline B of the team pipelines

Unzip this archive at `CT_GAT/` of the repository. It creates exactly what `python -m s02_preprocess.preprocess_full` writes by
default, so the loaders and Janice's model (`s03a_transformer/five_channel`,
`python -m experiments.train --model fivechannel --build CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs`) read it unchanged:

```
CT_GAT/processed/api_vocab.json              API vocabulary (ids >= FIRST_API_ID)
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/<sha256>.pt   one sample per binary (9)
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/<sha256>.manifest.json   per-sample alignment report
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/channel_embedder.pt      the seeded five-channel embedder
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/build_info/   index.csv, build_settings.json, build_summary.json, build_log.csv (not read by the code)
```

What is in a sample: `instruction_ids [N,5]` (opcode, operand 1, operand 2, API id, behaviour), `insn_to_block`,
`instruction_matched`, `block_features [n,77]`, `block_embeddings [n,64]`, `edge_index`, `edge_type`, `edge_attr`, `edge_back`,
`block_keys`, `label`, `dataset_metadata` (sample_id, label, arch, family, fold), and the rest of the keys `save_sample` writes.

How it was built: the 9 Mendeley x86 binaries of our 5-fold family-holdout set (3 ransomware,
6 goodware in this archive, no exclusions), `--sample signal`, budget 250 blocks, seed 0.

`signal` is the blocks of whole functions that call imports, highest signal first, up to the budget (several functions, so the result is not one connected subgraph).
Library functions are used only when a binary has no other code (they are collapsed in the IDA listing and cannot be matched).
CFGs come from the Mendeley bundle, listings from the Mendeley IDA export. Code: source `repo`, files of the repository when built:
- `CT_GAT/pipeline/s02_preprocess/preprocess_full.py`: sha256 `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- `CT_GAT/pipeline/s02_preprocess/tokenize_asm_gz.py`: sha256 `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`

Before training: `api_vocab.json` was grown over all binaries in one pass. The API rows the embedder added were drawn per (seed, API id) (`--seeded-rows`), so the table does not depend on a pause and resume of the build. Map API ids that do not occur in your training
binaries to `UNK_API` per fold (`--model fivechannel` and our team trainers do this), or rebuild the vocabulary from your training
split (`--split train`, then the other splits frozen).

`build_info/index.csv` lists, per binary: label, family, arch, our kfold fold, number of instructions, match rate (share of selected
instructions paired with a listing line), blocks in the binary and blocks kept.

cases.readme:
# Mendeley x86 CFG subgraphs (callwalk, 500 blocks), pipeline B of the team pipelines

Unzip this archive at `CT_GAT/` of the repository. It creates exactly what `python -m s02_preprocess.preprocess_full` writes by
default, so the loaders and Janice's model (`s03a_transformer/five_channel`,
`python -m experiments.train --model fivechannel --build CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs`) read it unchanged:

```
CT_GAT/processed/api_vocab.json              API vocabulary (ids >= FIRST_API_ID)
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/<sha256>.pt   one sample per binary (9)
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/channel_embedder.pt      the seeded five-channel embedder
CT_GAT/processed/cfg_subgraphs/build_info/   index.csv, build_settings.json, build_summary.json, build_log.csv (not read by the code)
```

(the per-sample manifest json files, alignment diagnostics that the models do not read, are left out of this archive; available on request)

What is in a sample: `instruction_ids [N,5]` (opcode, operand 1, operand 2, API id, behaviour), `insn_to_block`,
`instruction_matched`, `block_features [n,77]`, `block_embeddings [n,64]`, `edge_index`, `edge_type`, `edge_attr`, `edge_back`,
`block_keys`, `label`, `dataset_metadata` (sample_id, label, arch, family, fold), and the rest of the keys `save_sample` writes.

How it was built: the 10 Mendeley x86 binaries of our 5-fold family-holdout set (3 ransomware,
6 goodware in this archive, 1 excluded on purpose), `--sample callwalk`, budget 500 blocks, seed 3.

`callwalk` is a walk that grows from a seeded random block over the CFG edges and the call edges in both directions, with seeded restarts when the reachable region is smaller than the budget; the saved edges are the CFG edges among the chosen blocks.
Library functions are used only when a binary has no other code (they are collapsed in the IDA listing and cannot be matched).
CFGs come from the Mendeley bundle, listings from the Mendeley IDA export. Code: source `main-fix`

Before training: `api_vocab.json` was grown over all binaries in one pass. Map API ids that do not occur in your training
binaries to `UNK_API` per fold (`--model fivechannel` and our team trainers do this), or rebuild the vocabulary from your training
split (`--split train`, then the other splits frozen).

`build_info/index.csv` lists, per binary: label, family, arch, our kfold fold, number of instructions, match rate (share of selected
instructions paired with a listing line), blocks in the binary and blocks kept.
